QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_11

question.text: At Chenab Ventures' annual LP meeting, an LP asks why the GP received carry even though the fund IRR (pre-fees) is only 11% — below the LP's expected '20% of profit.' Assuming 8% pref, 100% catch-up and 80/20 split were met, the MOST appropriate manager response is:

answer.text: Carry was paid only because catch-up and 20% of distributable profit above pref were achieved; the LP still received its full capital plus 8% hurdle before GP carry began.
Carry is guaranteed to the GP regardless of hurdle; that is standard Indian AIF practice.
SEBI permits carry even where LPs lose money, provided the PPM discloses it.
Catch-up is applied before return of capital, so GP gets carry first and LPs recover later.

explanation.text: The Logic: In a European waterfall with 8% pref and 100% catch-up, the LP IS made whole on capital AND pref BEFORE GP receives any carry. Catch-up then brings the GP to a 20% cumulative share of profit; the 80/20 split applies beyond. An 11% fund IRR can still produce meaningful carry because the 3% above pref feeds the GP share. The Trap: Option B is factually wrong — no Indian PPM guarantees carry. Option C mis-states SEBI rules. Option D inverts the waterfall sequence. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test the waterfall conceptually from investor perspective. XIX-C expects the Manager to explain it LIVE to an LPAC — communication, not just math. Manager's Pro-Tip: At LP calls, always pair the waterfall explanation with a numerical table (capital out, pref received, GP carry, LP net). LPs who 'feel' ripped off usually stop feeling so the moment they see the columns.
